correctness.rationale: The integral unipotent matrix has determinant one and preserves Haar measure, so every starting time is stationary. The first orbit coordinate is x0+C(n,1)x1+C(n,2)x2+C(n,3)x3+C(n,4)alpha mod 1. The balanced half-circle sign has only odd nonzero Fourier harmonics and zero mean. In the Walsh moment for any nonempty subset of seven times, Haar integration over four independent coordinates kills all Fourier terms except integer relations sum_j c_j*C(j,r)=0 for r=0..3, where c_j are zero or odd. Equivalently C(z)=sum_j c_j z^j is divisible by (z-1)^4 with degree<=6. Writing C=(z-1)^4(a+bz+cz²), the coefficients at degrees 3,1,5 respectively are -4a+6b-4c, b-4a, b-4c. They are even, hence (if zero or odd) vanish; solving gives a=b=c=0. Therefore no nontrivial resonance; bounded Fejer approximants pass every moment limit in L1. Walsh inversion gives all 128 patterns exactly 1/128 for every alpha. Polynomial growth of T^n derivative yields polynomial Bowen spanning numbers and zero topological entropy, hence zero output entropy. Independent symbolic parity linear-algebra checks verified no polynomial relation and finite Fourier identity consistency; finite grids were not used to infer the Haar theorem.
residual_risks: Does not claim eight-block dependence, arbitrary seven-time independence or positive full-process entropy; Fejer convergence is justified by boundedness and Haar-uniform coordinates.
